newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY LEAGUE-Auckland consortium bid for NZ in ARL Cup.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-Auckland consortium bid for NZ in ARL Cup.

text.p: An Auckland-based consortium is behind a bid to field a New Zealand team in the Australian Rugby League's Optus Cup competition, former Kiwis coach Bob Bailey has confirmed, NZPA reported on Thursday.

Bailey declined to give details of his exact involvement, but said he believed a second New Zealand side could easily be marshalled to participate in the competition, rivalling the Super League-aligned Auckland Warriors.
Bailey was to have been coach of a New Zealand side dubbed the All Golds and initiated by the ARL to provide competition for the internationally isolated Australian team earlier this year.
ARL spokesman John Brady said consultations over a New Zealand side were "on-going".

Bailey said that while the idea was still in its infancy, an Auckland-based group was having regular discussions with the ARL and he believed there was enough depth within the game in New Zealand for a side other than the Warriors.
The issue of fielding new New Zealand and Melbourne sides had been placed on the agenda of an all-day conference of ARL officials held in Sydney this week, he said.
"It's really up to the ARL. The ball's in their court. It's early days yet, but I don't think we would have a problem putting a side together if they said 'go'," he said.
Bailey said it was too soon to say where such a side could be based -- Auckland, Wellington or Christchurch.
He declined to name other people involved in the discussions, but said several major companies had already expressed an interest.
Auckland Warriors founder Peter McLeod is a likely contender to be involved in a rival NZ side after he quit the club following the court decision in favour of Super League.
However, McLeod has said there were numerous groups in New Zealand wanting to start a new ARL team when Auckland first defected to Super League.
